title: Gallerie dell’Accademia: Masterpieces
subtitle: Twenty works in which architecture, crowds and intervals shape a story.
introduction:
In Carpaccio's Rialto painting, the miracle is easier to miss than the city. Boats, bridge and buildings claim attention around the episode that gives the work its name. That distribution offers a useful way into this selection: the apparent background often determines how slowly a story becomes visible and how widely its effects are imagined to spread.

Venetian streets and interiors organise several of these works, while ceiling compositions replace built enclosures with an opening into the sky. Giorgione's *Tempest* offers a different difficulty, leaving the relationship between its figures unresolved. The guide moves among these ways of locating an event, without assuming that every painting supplies one certain narrative answer.
visitNote: The guide covers selected works in the Gallerie dell’Accademia collection. Paintings may be on loan, and fragile drawings such as the Vitruvian Man are not part of a guaranteed permanent display. Check the museum’s current collection, exhibition and visiting information.

books.title: A Treatise on Painting
books.author: Leonardo da Vinci; translated by John Francis Rigaud
books.note: Leonardo’s writings on proportion, perspective and movement accompany the questions raised by the Vitruvian Man. The book also provides terms for comparing the measured city views with Tintoretto’s foreshortened bodies.

works.title: Miracle of the True Cross at the Rialto Bridge
works.catalogueTitle: The Miracle of the Relic of the True Cross on the Rialto Bridge
works.credit: Vittore Carpaccio. The Miracle of the Relic of the True Cross on the Rialto Bridge. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/vittore-carpaccio/the-miracle-of-the-relic-of-the-true-cross-on-the-rialto-bridge-1494
works.description: Gondolas and the old wooden bridge make the canal immediately conspicuous. The miraculous episode occupies a much smaller place at the upper left. Carpaccio allows the city to sustain activities beyond the named story. The work can be read as a sacred event situated within public life, rather than a city emptied out to provide its backdrop.

works.title: Feast in the House of Levi
works.catalogueTitle: Feast in the House of Levi (Last Supper)
works.credit: Feast in the House of Levi (Last Supper). WikiArt; Paolo Veronese. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: Three great arches give the banquet an expansive structure, but they do not keep attention fixed at the central table. Servants, animals and peripheral figures repeatedly draw the eye elsewhere. Veronese makes the surrounding social world part of the meal's presentation. Architecture holds the gathering together while allowing several incidents to compete within it.

works.title: Arrival of the English Ambassadors
works.catalogueTitle: The Arrival of the English Ambassadors
works.credit: Vittore Carpaccio. The Arrival of the English Ambassadors. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/vittore-carpaccio/the-arrival-of-the-english-ambassadors-1498
works.description: Halls, steps and openings separate groups while keeping passages between them visible. Carpaccio uses architecture to organise moments in a narrative, asking the eye to move rather than settle at one central encounter. The buildings have a temporal role as well as a spatial one. Crossing the painted room can mean advancing through the story.

works.title: The Transport of the Holy House of Nazareth to Loreto
works.catalogueTitle: Transportation of the Holy House of Nazareth to Loreto
works.credit: Transportation of the Holy House of Nazareth to Loreto. WikiArt; Giovanni Battista Tiepolo. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: Masonry enters an arrangement of clouds, angels and airborne drapery. Tiepolo makes the miraculous transport intelligible through a contradiction between the building's implied weight and its diagonal movement across the oval field. The surrounding figures help carry that improbable relation. The house remains substantial enough for its suspension to matter.

works.title: The Coronation of the Virgin
works.catalogueTitle: Coronation of the Virgin
works.credit: Michele Giambono. Coronation of the Virgin. Image credit: Michele Giambono. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Repeated heads, haloes and levels organise the dense assembly around the elevated Christ and Mary. Giambono gives heaven a ceremonial order without needing a naturalistic room. Gold and red bind the ranks together while individual figures remain identifiable. The picture's crowded surface communicates hierarchy through placement rather than through ordinary distances between bodies.

works.title: The Crucifixion
works.catalogueTitle: Crucifixion
works.credit: Andrea Previtali. Crucifixion. Image credit: Didier Descouens. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The cross connects the immediate group of mourners to an extensive landscape. Previtali leaves room around the event, allowing changes of light to distinguish the hill from the farther terrain. The vertical holds the scene together without requiring the people to fill it. The place continues beyond the subject at its centre.

works.title: The Finding of Jesus in the Temple
works.catalogueTitle: Finding of Jesus in the Temple
works.credit: Giovanni Antonio Fumiani. Finding of Jesus in the Temple. Image credit: Didier Descouens. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The child occupies only part of an imposing gathering among columns and steps. Fumiani makes the surrounding institution physically large while directing its figures into argument and attention. Gestures prevent the architecture from becoming a merely formal display. The difference between Jesus's bodily scale and the response around him makes the subject legible.

works.title: Saint Dominic in Glory
works.catalogueTitle: Giambattista Tiepolo, San Domenico in gloria
works.credit: Giovanni Battista Tiepolo. Giambattista Tiepolo, San Domenico in gloria. Image credit: Didier Descouens. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Shortened views of limbs suggest bodies seen from below, while pale openings break through darker figures near the edges. Tiepolo's ceiling arrangement asks the painted space to continue above the viewer rather than recede like a window on a wall. A flat reproduction preserves the design but cannot fully reproduce that intended bodily position beneath it.

works.title: The Tempest
works.catalogueTitle: La tempesta
works.credit: Giorgione. La tempesta. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Lightning links the unsettled sky to a landscape divided between the standing man and nursing woman. Their relationship is not explained by a decisive shared action. Giorgione gives the intervening ground, ruins and distant buildings substantial attention. The painting remains available for precise description even when no single narrative interpretation can be stated as certain.

works.title: Vitruvian Man
works.catalogueTitle: The proportions of the human figure (The Vitruvian Man)
works.credit: Leonardo da Vinci. The proportions of the human figure (The Vitruvian Man). Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The superimposed arms and legs do not represent one stationary pose. Leonardo compares bodily proportions with a circle and square through different positions, accompanied by written notes. The familiar emblem is therefore also a working diagram. The original drawing is not a permanent-display attraction: conservation limits access, so any opportunity to see it must be confirmed separately.

works.title: Miracle of the Relic of the Holy Cross
works.catalogueTitle: Miracle of the Relic of the Holy Cross
works.credit: Benedetto Rusconi. Miracle of the Relic of the Holy Cross. Image credit: Didier Descouens. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The small group, including a child, occupies the lower part of an unusually tall architectural setting. Benedetto Diana makes discovery of the action slower by allowing arch and wall to command so much space. The human episode gains a spacious frame rather than a close-up. Scale changes how the event is approached before its details are understood.

works.title: Miracle of the Cross at Campo San Lio
works.catalogueTitle: Miracle of the Relic of the Holy Cross in Campo San Lio
works.credit: Giovanni di Niccolò Mansueti. Miracle of the Relic of the Holy Cross in Campo San Lio. Image credit: Didier Descouens. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: White garments create a conspicuous band through the crowded square. Around the procession, spectators and detailed façades locate devotion within an urban community. Mansueti makes the ceremony's public character visible through repetition and watching. The event includes those taking part and those whose presence turns it into something collectively witnessed.

works.title: The Raising of Lazarus
works.catalogueTitle: Resurrection of Lazarus
works.credit: Leandro Bassano. Resurrection of Lazarus. Image credit: Didier Descouens. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Hands reach and bodies bend around the pale figure close to the ground. Leandro Bassano lets light distinguish this crowded activity from the darker architecture above it. The miracle emerges through physical relations rather than an isolated emblem of divine power. The lower space remains a place of support and effort as the event unfolds.

works.title: The Assumption of the Virgin
works.catalogueTitle: The Assumption of the Virgin
works.credit: Palma Vecchio. The Assumption of the Virgin. Image credit: Palma Vecchio; https://www.gallerieaccademia.it/assunzione-della-vergine. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:315_Palma_il_Vecchio_Assunzione_della_Vergine_(trsp).png. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: The apostles look and gesture upwards across the gap separating them from Mary. Palma Vecchio makes that interval active: it records distance while carrying a continuous exchange of attention. Earthly witnesses and the ascending figure occupy different levels, yet neither group becomes a self-contained scene. Their relation supplies the composition's direction.

works.title: The Healing of the Daughter of Benvegnudo of San Polo
works.catalogueTitle: The Miraculous Healing of the Daughter of Benvegnudo of San Polo
works.credit: Giovanni di Niccolò Mansueti. The Miraculous Healing of the Daughter of Benvegnudo of San Polo. Image credit: Didier Descouens. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: A broad staircase divides the interior and gives witnesses several positions from which to attend to the gathering below. Mansueti makes a household's architecture distribute the event beyond its immediate participants. The healing acquires reach through passages and levels. The building organises who can see and how separate groups belong to one scene.

works.title: The Relic of the Holy Cross Offered to the Scuola di San Giovanni Evangelista
works.catalogueTitle: The Relic of the Holy Cross is offered to the Scuola Grande di San Giovanni Evangelista
works.credit: Lazzaro Bastiani. The Relic of the Holy Cross is offered to the Scuola Grande di San Giovanni Evangelista. Image credit: Didier Descouens. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Contrasting robes distinguish participants in a ceremonial exchange before the church and adjoining buildings. Bastiani gives the institution's defining ritual a public location rather than an abstract ceremonial field. Architecture helps stabilise an account of collective memory. The exchange is presented as something belonging to the city as well as to the people immediately involved.

works.title: The Soothsayer
works.catalogueTitle: The Soothsayer
works.credit: Pietro Longhi. The Soothsayer. Image credit: Didier Descouens. Wikimedia Commons. CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Some faces are masked while others remain visible around the fortune-teller. Longhi gives the social gathering as much attention as the promise of prediction. The masks introduce a useful complication: people seeking knowledge participate while withholding parts of their own appearance. Bright clothes and dark headwear keep the small groups distinct inside that exchange.

works.title: The Dream of Saint Ursula
works.catalogueTitle: Dream of St.Ursula
works.credit: Vittore Carpaccio. Dream of St.Ursula. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Tiles, windows and furnishings establish the room before the entering angel alters its ordinary use. Carpaccio places a visionary subject within a carefully measured interior, with Ursula asleep rather than actively receiving a visitor. The setting's plausibility sharpens the difference introduced at the doorway. A dream is given the physical organisation of household space.

works.title: Self-Portrait
works.catalogueTitle: Self-Portrait
works.credit: Rosalba Carriera. Self-Portrait. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Carriera's pale face emerges through small tonal differences beneath grey hair. Soft edges join skin and clothing without making the likeness indistinct. The pastel offers a direct encounter that does not depend on a hard continuous contour. Attention belongs to the particular transitions around the features rather than an idealised, uniformly smooth account of the face.

works.title: The Miracle of Saint Mark Freeing the Slave
works.catalogueTitle: The Miracle of St Mark Freeing the Slave
works.credit: Tintoretto. The Miracle of St Mark Freeing the Slave. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The plunging saint and horizontal body establish opposing axes across the central space. Tintoretto makes the gap between heaven and earth a path of action, with onlookers responding through markedly different gestures. The extreme bodily angles distinguish intervention from spectatorship. The miracle's force is carried through the arrangement before the surrounding crowd is read person by person.

closingSections.title: Let the setting take time
paragraphs: In the narrative paintings, follow a staircase, a canal or an opening before searching for the named protagonist. Architecture often explains how the event is shared. Check current displays and special exhibitions before visiting, particularly for works on paper such as Leonardo's drawing.
